US_behavior: natural adaptation: preserve the now-secure seam, mass M4A2 + engineers + 75-mm + naval direct fire + CVE spotting against identified strongpoints, and avoid broad unsupported infantry pushes. Fire is efficient but not omniscient; hidden firing slits, false damage assessment and local coordination failures persist.

US_ground_state.logistics: verified lanes plus repaired LVT/LCM shuttle make ammunition, water, engineer stores and evacuation reliable enough for deliberate reduction warfare
US_ground_state.Green_Beach: centered secured for useful logistics during afternoon after costly western strongpoint reduction; not instantly safe at dawn

Japanese_ground_state.C2: islandwide command mostly fragmented; strongpoint wire/runners/local ammunition continue to make individual pockets tougher than the aggregate command picture suggests
Japanese_ground_state.doctrine: no new mass banzai charge; surviving tanks used as short-hop mobile firepoints and local counter-move reserve

progress: Morning: US reduces the Red 2/3-adjacent and central-airfield strongpoints systematically; Japanese positions can still inflict losses but lose mutual support.

Midday-afternoon: western/southwestern positions that benefited from the pre-GALVANIC defensive bias are reduced with tanks, engineers and destroyer/direct fire; Green Beach becomes increasingly useful.
Late day: eastern/northern and selected inland strongpoints remain organized. The island is not declared secure and high-intensity CVE/spotting demand continues into 27 Nov.

T24_state.assessment: US victory on Betio is structurally certain, but organized resistance remains sufficient to demand another full reduction day. Do not close Tarawa on old 11/28/29 clocks yet; propagate from this state.
